Definition: from G1537 and G2806; to exscind:--break off.
BiblicalUsage: To break off is to cut a branch from a tree, and Paul uses it for the branches of Israel broken off from the olive tree. If some of the branches were broken off, and you, a wild olive tree, were grafted in among them, he says, do not boast against the branches, because they were broken off through unbelief, and you stand by faith. The word is a warning to every branch that forgets it did not plant itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God can break off and graft in, because the tree is His and the branches are held by faith, not by birth. I hold that I stand only by faith, and if I forget that, I forget everything.
